title: Binary compatibility certification checklist for onprem artifacts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and playbook to certify binary and package compatibility for private (VPC / on-prem) runtime artifacts prior to rollout. Focus: ensure deterministic artifact verification, cross-hardware ABI sanity, terraform module compatibility, and safe rollback knobs.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers: container images, deb/rpm packages, prebuilt runtime binaries, TF modules, and appliance tarballs.
- Assumes customers run a mix of NVIDIA + AMD GPUs and heterogenous CPU kernels.
- Not covering: model weights format migration (separate doc).
- Goal: shrink unknowns that caused past flaky upgrades.

High level flow (certification path):
1) Build -> deterministic output (CI reproducible)
2) Sign -> cosign/GPG/HSM signature stored with provenance metadata
3) Smoke -> basic health checks on a small staging fleet (kube, systemd)
4) Compatibility tests -> ABI + kernel-level smoke across target hardware families
5) TF/Infra validation -> terraform plan/apply dry-run + module compatibility checks
6) Canary rollout -> traffic-slice + telemetry gating -> escalate or rollback
7) Final sign-off -> ship to private registry / AWS S3 / appliance image repository

Checklist (concrete steps and commands):
- Build reproducibility
  - Ensure CI job uses pinned toolchain (gcc/clang, go, python). Document exact tool versions in artifact metadata.
  - Hash outputs: sha256sum <artifact> -> store value in release metadata.
  - Example: sha256sum redwood-runtime-v2.3.1-linux-amd64.tar.gz 

- Signing and provenance
  - Container images: cosign sign --key k8s://<kms-uri> <registry>/runtime:v2.3.1
  - Tarballs/debs: gpg --batch --yes --detach-sign -o file.sig file.tar.gz ; publish .sig next to artifact.
  - Store provenance JSON with: builder commit, build env, build date, checksum, component list, linked tf module version.
  - Verify with cosign/openssl/gpg during install: cosign verify <image> ; gpg --verify file.sig file.tar.gz

- Cross-hardware ABI compatibility tests
  - Produce a tiny compatibility harness that loads binary and exercises expected dynamic symbols and memory APIs. (linker/ldd, nm checks)
  - On target nodes: ldd /opt/redwood/bin/runtime-agent | grep 'not found' -> fail if unresolved libs.
  - Run short workload: ./compat-harness --model small --seq 32 --tokens 64 --iterations 10 --check-kvcache
  - Collect exit code, stderr, perf counters (nvidia-smi / rocm-smi) and attach to run record.

- Kernel and driver gating
  - Verify NVIDIA driver >= recommended and docker runtime supports required CUDA version. List supported driver versions in artifact metadata.
  - For AMD/ROCm, ensure kernel modules loaded and environment variables (HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES) behave as expected.

- Terraform module validation and state compatibility
  - Maintain a test workspace per customer pattern. Run: terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars -out=plan.out
  - Validate module version pinning: grep -R "module .*source" modules/ -> ensure tags, not master.
  - Detect deprecation: run tf provider schema diff script (link to script in linked_artifacts)
  - Example check: terraform state list | grep redwood_runtime -> record resource names for state-migration playbook.
  - If module changes rename resources, provide state-migration mapping: terraform state mv old.resource new.resource (document mapping in release notes)

- Configuration and API contract compatibility sanity
  - API shim: provide backward-compatible /api/legacy endpoints when removing or renaming fields.
  - Integration test: run curl -fsS --fail against /v1/health and legacy endpoints; run unit smoke for header parsing differences.
  - Schema evolution: allow unknown fields by default for config.yaml parsing to avoid failures; log warnings for deprecated keys.

- Observability and telemetry gating
  - Enable 1% sample telemetry by default in staging. Collect: latency p95/p50, token-cost delta, error-rate, cpu/gpu utilization, queue depth.
  - Pre-compare baseline: run baseline job that executes representative prompt set and store metrics.
  - Define gating rules: fail canary if error-rate > baseline * 2 OR p95 latency regress > 25% OR token-cost delta > 15%.

- Canary rollout plan (safety-first)
  - Phase 0: silent canary (no production traffic) on 3 nodes across AZs; validate logs and metrics 24h.
  - Phase 1: 0.5% traffic slice for 1h -> check gating rules.
  - Phase 2: 5% traffic slice for 4h -> automated rollback if gating hit.
  - Phase 3: 25% for 24h -> human-in-loop approval.
  - Phase 4: full rollout with 10% step increases every 30m if healthy.
  - Rollback commands: kubectl rollout undo deploy/runtime -n redwood --to-revision=<prev> OR image rollback via registry tag (use pinned digest). For appliance: switch symlink from /opt/runtime/current -> /opt/runtime/<prev>.

- Artifact pinning and digest usage (critical)
  - Always pin container images by digest in TF and k8s manifests: image: registry/realtime/runtime@sha256:<digest>
  - For packages, reference artifact checksum in TF module variable (artifact_checksum = "sha256:...") to prevent accidental drift.

- Offline/airgapped delivery considerations
  - Provide signed tarball + .sig + provenance json. Include a small verification script that runs cosign/gpg openssl verification without external network.
  - Provide dependency list with vendor copies for apt/yum or a local yum repo.

- Automation and CI checks to add to repo (TODOs)
  - CI job: artifact-provenance-generator -> writes provenance JSON and uploads to signed bucket.
  - CI job: cross-arch-compat-smoke -> spin small VMs for amd64/arm64 + nvidia/rocm shim tests.
  - Terraform drift detector: nightly run that compares live plan with expected resources and alerts channel.

- Examples and commands to include in final KB
  - cosign sign/verify examples, gpg sign/verify, sha256sum examples.
  - terraform plan -> save plan.out -> terraform show -json plan.out > plan.json -> run diff script.
  - kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime -n redwood --timeout=10m

Open questions / risks to resolve:
- Which key management option becomes the default for private customers: HSM-backed cosign keys or customer-provided GPG? (security wants HSM by default for enterprise)
- Snapshotting terraform state for customers where module renames are required: do we run state migration for them or provide step-by-step instructions? (operations time vs customer autonomy)
- How do we measure subtle quality regressions introduced by quantization or kernel changes that don't show up in token-level errors? (need human-eval sets + automated evals)

Release timeline template (example):
- Week -2: run full reproducible build, produce artifacts, sign artifacts, run smoke tests.
- Week -1: cross-hardware compatibility tests + tf validation against staging customer workspace.
- Week 0: staged canary rollout (phased).
- Week +1: finalize and publish KB, mirror signed artifacts to regional buckets.

Owners and contacts:
- Lead: Claire Zhang (eng-private-deployments)
- Compatibility tests owner: Samir Patel (applied-ml infra)
- TF / infra: Jordan Lee (platform-engineering)
- Security / signing consult: Priya Menon (security)

Notes to self (short):
- Keep this intentionally procedural. Capture commands that on-call can run without hunting for docs.
- Add a minimal offline verification script to repo before next alpha.
- After first rollout, capture lessons and convert checklist to a release automation playbook.

Appendix: quick verification snippets
- Verify image digest locally: 
  docker pull registry/runtime:v2.3.1 && docker inspect --format='{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' registry/runtime:v2.3.1
- Example cosign verify: cosign verify --key k8s://projects/_/keys/cosign-key projects.gcr.io/runtime@sha256:...
- Example gpg verify: gpg --keyring ./trustedkeys.gpg --verify runtime.tar.gz.sig runtime.tar.gz

End of working draft.
